scope: Acceptance infrastructure for the current checked compiler subset; no universal compatibility claim
phase1Scope: Lexical and ownership foundation corpus, error recovery, explicit React reference feasibility blockers; not universal compatibility or React error-boundary semantics
phase2Scope: Derived-value and control-flow corpus: gated nested branches, same-element identity, fragments, root ranges and supported early returns; not universal compatibility or later-phase effects, composition and lists
phase3Scope: Passive-effect increment: inline useEffect callbacks with literal empty dependencies retain initial snapshots; direct state dependencies in nonempty literal arrays use owned dependency watchers with per-setup captures, cleanup ordering and passive scheduling; omitted dependencies, callback indirection and broader effect forms remain open
phase4Scope: Composition corpus for direct local function components: reactive/destructured/static-default props, inline callbacks, one lazy child or primitive render-prop result, direct local context providers and consumers, conditional context snapshots, independent roots, local forwardRef wrappers, direct local tuple custom hooks, thrown setup cleanup and ref disposal; broader component forms remain open
phase5Scope: Direct-operation list corpus: source-visible functional or event-snapshot append/filter, functional prepend, immutable splice/sort/reverse, exact tail removal and clear update an owned mapped region with reactive indices and operation traces, without old/new keyed matching; map updates require a statically preserved direct-property key, native sort/splice edge coercions are covered, repeated event-snapshot appends share one captured predecessor, functional operation chains retain direct provenance, and lexical binding identity rejects shadowed replacements; seeded sequences plus identical-source browser checks cover row identity, focus, selection and focus-event traces; opaque replacements remain unsupported
phase6Scope: The unchanged flip issue application under React 19.2 and the strict target: an exact-path manual module-contract manifest, import-source/export-aware aliases, changing issue effects, direct operation props, copied slice move provenance, forms, context, routes and fixed source maps; local tarball ESM, declaration, strict-compiler and production-bundle checks cover the package shape; this remains a bounded application result
phase7Scope: Native SVG and direct portal compatibility slices: compiler-declared SVG/foreignObject namespace context, tested SVG attributes, and portal placement/ownership with reactive values, events, conditional children, stable identity and post-unmount inactivity in independently built React 19.2 and strict-target browser fixtures; changing portal targets, portal keys, cross-component SVG context and broader semantics remain unsupported
explicitLimits: Phase 2 verifies only the recorded derived-value and control-flow corpus; effects, component composition, opaque list inputs and universal React compatibility remain open.
Phase 1 error tests establish runtime recovery and ownership, not React error-boundary, retry, concurrent or passive-error semantics.
Phase 1 reference counterexamples remain unsupported by the target; successful rejection tests do not fulfill P4.
Runtime entry tracing detects the project's known reconciler; novel or opaque matching algorithms require source review.
Body probes plus source review guard against disguised replay; probes alone are not a semantic proof.
Production module checks do not identify React embedded anonymously in a third-party vendored bundle.
Browser compares rendered text, properties, focus, selection and identity; internal empty text/comment anchors remain observable differences.
The displayed body-execution counter is excluded from React text equality and independently asserted as one for the target.

Only direct inline useEffect callbacks are supported by the strict compiler, with a literal dependency array or none. Empty arrays retain initial snapshots; nonempty arrays currently support direct state dependencies through owned watchers. An omitted array is inferred from the reactive bindings the callback reads, so the effect re-runs when one of them changes rather than after every render, and runs once when it reads none. Callback indirection, non-literal dependency arguments, layout effects, broader dependency expressions and broader scheduling remain unsupported.

Composition accepts bounded direct-local forms only: one child, primitive render-prop results, direct local createContext/forwardRef/custom tuple hooks and inline callbacks. Spreads, keys, multiple children, imported/member components, general wrapper or hook analysis, retained callback identity and arbitrary JSX returned by render props remain unsupported.

Direct-operation lists currently accept only source-visible functional or event-snapshot append/filter/map, functional prepend, toSpliced, toSorted, toReversed, the exact copied-array two-splice move (spread or zero-argument slice copy), exact previous.slice(0, -1) tail removal and setState([]) clear forms. Provenance crosses direct local getter props and explicitly declared imported operation props. Map publication requires a direct-property JSX key and a mapper statically proven to preserve it; mutable-field callback locals are rejected pending row-owned reactive compilation. Repeated direct appends from one event snapshot may supersede the immediately preceding append from that snapshot. Other skipped-predecessor chains, opaque replacement arrays and updater syntax outside these forms remain unsupported.

Phase 6 module facts come from a manually asserted exact-path manifest. Automatic module-graph extraction and validation of dependency implementations, general imported hooks/components, SSR, hydration, concurrency and broad React semantics remain outside this result.

The fresh consumer installs local tarballs and verifies ESM, declarations, strict compilation and a production bundle; that each packed dist/ equals a fresh compile of its package source; that a Node process importing the packages ends by itself after a passive effect has run; and that require() and synchronous Babel with the plugin named in configuration work. It does not publish packages, test a public registry install or establish compatibility for unsupported source forms.

The Phase 7 SVG slice supports namespace context visible within one compiled JSX tree plus the tested attribute aliases. SVG children returned through a component boundary, namespaced JSX syntax and the broader SVG attribute/event surface remain unsupported.

The Phase 7 portal slice supports a named createPortal import, a stable captured Element/DocumentFragment target, direct portal content, conditional removal/restoration and owner cleanup. Portal keys, changing targets, default/namespace react-dom imports, cross-root ownership and broader React portal event propagation semantics remain unsupported.
